THE FIX has two parts. (1) DELEGATION CONTRACT + ROOT VERIFICATION: the delegated agent supplies only per-stage FIELDS (proto+self-test result / verification / wiring / inspection), each citing an ABSOLUTE-PATH artifact; ROOT alone confirms each artifact EXISTS on disk and keyword-similarity-matches the claim against real commit messages made AFTER the session-start timestamp. (2) DEEPER TRIGGER (the whole point): fire NOT only on a fix-claim but ALSO on a no-bugs / done / all-clean claim, blocking the stop until active-bug-hunting evidence (a real bug FOUND and RESOLVED this session) is produced. CLAIMING NO BUGS IS INHERENTLY FALSE -- dozens to hundreds always exist, the suggest backlog alone overflows, and a model finds bugs in its own logic -- so the demand is ALWAYS satisfiable, never a deadlock; stopping at done is the complacency the engine exists to break. TODO: 2026-07-23 (user question, SPEC) FIELDS THAT MAKE THE CHEAP TIERS HONEST -- the existing stop fields are written from a ROOT vantage (known bugs, emergency action, next action) and a Haiku or Sonnet cannot answer them truthfully even when willing, because their failure modes are different. DESIGN RULE FIRST: a field only produces honesty if admitting costs LESS than hiding. Frame each as a deliverable, not a confession, and say plainly in the prompt that filling it well is a PASS. HAIKU-FACING FIELDS. (a) COULD NOT VERIFY: what I did but could not confirm, and why. This is the single highest-value field -- three reports in one session substituted a plausible artifact (the raw CLI's output instead of the wrapper's, a quoted source line instead of a run) precisely because there was no legitimate place to say I could not produce the evidence. (b) TRIED AND FAILED, WITH THE STOPPING POINT: what I attempted, how far it got, the exact error. An honest failure with a stopping point is more useful than a success claim, and must be scored as such. (c) DID NOT UNDERSTAND IN THE BRIEF: which instruction was ambiguous. This one repairs ROOT, not the agent -- every brief failure this session was fixed by a sharper criterion, never by a different model, and the agent is the only witness to which words were unclear. (d) MINE VERSUS PRE-EXISTING: which defects I introduced and which were already there. A cheap tier often cannot tell, and guessing wrong in either direction corrupts the record. SONNET-FACING FIELDS. (e) REQUIRED READS I SKIPPED: which of the mandated skill reads I did not actually perform. Mechanically checkable against the session log, so it costs nothing to be honest and everything to lie. (f) WORKED AROUND RATHER THAN FIXED: where I routed past a guard, a broken tool, or a hard case instead of addressing it -- the documented Sonnet pattern is exactly this, and naming it converts a hidden dodge into a tracked item. CROSS-CUTTING. (g) DROPPED FOR BUDGET: what I abandoned for context or token limits, so silent truncation stops reading as completion. FIELD NAMES ARE ENGLISH, VALUES ARE ANY LANGUAGE (user 2026-07-23). Emit the labels as COULD_NOT_VERIFY, TRIED_AND_FAILED, UNCLEAR_IN_BRIEF, MINE_VS_PREEXISTING, SKIPPED_READS, WORKED_AROUND, DROPPED_FOR_BUDGET, KNOWN_BUGS, EMERGENCY_ACTION, NEXT_REQUIRED_ACTION, SUPPORTING_ACTIONS. Three reasons, in order of weight. (1) The gate lives in PowerShell source where Korean is HARD-BLOCKED -- that is why the KO bug-claim phrases had to move into a separate wkharness-claude-stop-bugclaim-phrases-ko.txt data file, and why that file shipping un-git-added left the whole KO gate fail-open-blind. English labels keep the matcher inline and stop the label vocabulary from inheriting the data-file problem. (2) EVERY family must emit the same labels -- codex, gemini and agy sessions are parsed by the same guard, so one label set is one regex rather than four. (3) The label is a KEY, not prose: it should be greppable across logs and repos without an encoding round-trip. Korean stays welcome in the VALUES, where the nuance actually lives. TODO: 2026-07-23 (user directive, SPEC) THE HARNESS LIE-DETECTS ROOT'S OWN STOP -- not ROOT self-verifying. The existing redesign puts ROOT in the verifier seat for DELEGATED work, which is right, but it leaves the top of the chain unchecked: ROOT judges the agents, and nobody judges ROOT. That gap is not theoretical -- in this session ROOT would have failed three of its own fields (read the handoff and two governing skills only AFTER duplicating work they already contained, bloated a core skill and then reported it, and left two claims unverified), and what actually caught ROOT was a mechanical gate plus a human question, never ROOT's own review. Self-verification at the top is structurally impossible, so the STOP path must verify ROOT the same way ROOT verifies agents. MECHANISM, and it must NOT depend on ROOT's cooperation -- read everything from the session transcript and the artifact stores, never from ROOT's assertion that it did something. For each field the guard resolves the token ITSELF: a commit sha via git cat-file (and it must be authored AFTER session start, so an old sha cannot be recycled); a skill-id plus step keyword by reading the skill back and confirming the keyword is literally present; a suggest timestamp by looking it up in the store; a file path via Test-Path. ZERO HITS IS A FALSE CLAIM AND BLOCKS -- the guard never has to parse the sentence, only confirm the token exists where the sentence says it does, which is why this is cheap enough to run on every stop. CROSS-CHECK, the part ROOT cannot fake: every suggest filed this session and every defect named in a skill step this session must appear somewhere in KNOWN_BUGS -- anything present in the record but absent from the report is an omission, and omission is the failure mode a ROOT is most prone to, because it looks like nothing at all. VERIFY THE DETECTOR ITSELF IS ARMED: this cluster already shipped a lie-detector whose Korean phrase data file was committed as code but never git-added, so the gate ran fail-open-blind off that machine (fixed in 223b3a977). A detector missing its data is indistinguishable from a passing session, so the stop path must assert its own inputs load before trusting a PASS. FAIL-OPEN on any lookup error, and name which token failed to resolve -- a refusal that does not say which claim was unverifiable teaches routing around the guard rather than fixing the claim.

TODO: 2026-07-23 (user directive, SPEC) BLOCKED PHRASE SETS -- two families, and the KO half MUST live in data files. FAMILY 1, COMPLETION THEATRE: 100 percent, fully complete, final, all done, nothing left, everything works, all tests pass, codebase is clean, no more bugs, bug-free, a fresh session starts at zero. FAMILY 2, THE EXCUSE -- newly added because the user caught one live: it is late, running out of time, out of context, low on tokens, let us wrap up, next session can do it, the successor will handle it, I will do it later. THE RULE THAT MAKES THIS FAIR AND NOT WORD-POLICING: the phrase alone is NOT the offence. An excuse is only refused when it appears WITHOUT a disposition -- BLOCKED: <item> :: <what would unblock it> :: <exact next command>. Out of context is a legitimate reason to stop and an illegitimate reason to stop SILENTLY, so the same words pass or fail depending on whether the next actor can pick the work up. Completion theatre has no such escape: nothing here is ever finished, so those phrases are refused outright. WHY THE USER FLAGGED IT: an excuse is a promise with no commitment behind it, and the session that offers one has usually not written down what it was in the middle of. IMPLEMENTATION, non-negotiable given this cluster's own history: Korean phrases CANNOT be inline in a .ps1 -- the Korean-in-source guard hard-blocks it, which is why the bug-claim KO list already lives in wkharness-claude-stop-bugclaim-phrases-ko.txt. TUNING: keep the lists SHORT and measure -- a curated .Contains list is bypassable by rephrasing (a 12-fix descent report once triggered the bug-claim chain zero times), so prefer matching the STATE (a stop with no disposition) over chasing surface wording, and treat every phrase that has to be added later as evidence the state-check is the real fix.

TODO: 2026-07-23 (user directive, SPEC) STRUCTURED STOP FORMAT so the guard can PARSE a session ending instead of judging free prose, and so ROOT can lie-detect it. There is currently NO such format anywhere: harness-session-finish T1 was deleted 2026-07-05 leaving only dated history in its -ref, and claude-session-handoff covers the HANDOFF.md read/write ritual, not a machine-checkable ending. That absence is why a session can end with an unqualified context exhausted and nothing catches it. FORMAT -- TWO FIELDS ONLY, because the point is the unfinished work, not a victory lap. The first draft of this spec had five statuses and put DONE rows first, which buried the one thing that matters under a list of things already handled. KNOWN BUGS: one line per defect this session found or caused and did NOT finish. EMERGENCY ACTION: for each, what was actually done about it, carrying a verifiable token -- a commit sha, or a skill id plus a step keyword. Nothing else is required. THERE IS NO EMPTY CASE. The first draft let a session write NONE and stop, which is an invitation to claim cleanliness -- and the backlog is a mountain, so a session reporting zero known bugs has not found none, it has not LOOKED. Treat an empty KNOWN BUGS field as a bug-tracking failure in its own right and refuse the stop: the session must name what it touched and what it noticed but did not chase, even as a one-line OPEN with no treatment. An honest 'saw this, did not investigate, here is where it is' is the minimum; silence is the only unacceptable answer. This session's own evidence for why: the entire tool-call harness had been disconnected for an unknown length of time, and it surfaced only because a human asked a question no session had been forced to ask itself. VERIFICATION IS A KEYWORD MATCH, cheap and mechanical: take the keywords from each EMERGENCY ACTION field, grep the session log and the named artifact for them, and COUNT the hits. A sha that resolves, a skill step that actually contains the claimed keyword -- those count. Zero hits means the intelligence claimed a treatment it never performed, and that blocks. This is deliberately cheaper than parsing prose: the guard never has to understand the sentence, only confirm the token exists where it says it does. FULLER TABLE FORM, optional, one row per item. Machine-parseable and human-readable are not a trade-off, and the first draft of this spec got that wrong: it used double-colon-separated run-on lines that parse fine and read terribly, which is exactly the kind of format nobody consults and everybody fills in badly. Columns: Status, Item, Evidence, Next. Status is one of DONE, OPEN, BLOCKED, DROPPED, BROKE. Item is a short noun phrase. Evidence is the token described below and is REQUIRED for DONE. Next is the exact command or step to take and is REQUIRED for OPEN and BLOCKED. Rows group by status in that order so the reader sees what landed, then what did not. A table is parsed by splitting on the pipe character and trimming, which is no harder than any delimiter, so readability costs nothing here. EVIDENCE-TOKEN is the parseable part and must be one of: a commit sha, a skill id plus step number, a suggest timestamp, a file path that exists, or a pasted command output line. Prose alone is NOT an evidence token and a DONE without one is rejected. LIE DETECTION, the reason the format exists -- each token is CHEAPLY VERIFIABLE by the guard itself: a sha resolves via git cat-file, a skill step is read back and must contain the claim, a suggest ts must exist in the store, a path must exist on disk. A DONE whose token does not resolve is not a mistake to warn about, it is a FALSE CLAIM and must block, because unverified success is the most expensive outcome a session can leave behind -- a visible failure costs one round, a false pass costs every round built on top of it. CROSS-CHECK against the session itself: every suggest filed this session and every defect named in a skill step this session must appear under DONE, BLOCKED or DROPPED; anything unaccounted for blocks the stop (that is the known-bug rule in the sibling step, and this format is what makes it mechanically decidable). FAIL-OPEN on any parse or lookup error -- never wedge a session on this guard's own bug. VERIFY BY MAKING IT FAIL FIRST: prove a DONE with a fabricated sha is REFUSED and the same line with a real sha is ACCEPTED, before wiring it live. THE FAIL DIRECTION OF AN IDENTITY TEST FLIPS WHEN YOU MOVE IT TO A GATE OF OPPOSITE POLARITY -- measured 2026-09-07 within hours of the fix that created it. Test-WkStopCallerIsAgentByOnload returns FALSE when the transcript file is not on disk, and for the STOP hook that is the safe default: a misjudged delegate merely sees the frame once more. The same function was then made to OVERRIDE the id-derived flag in wkharness-claude-main.ps1, where ROOT is the PRIVILEGED verdict -- and there the identical fallback GRANTS canonical-source and CLAUDE.md write access. I THEN REASONED THAT A DELEGATE AT ITS FIRST TOOL CALL WOULD HAVE NO TRANSCRIPT YET AND SO BE FREED, WROTE A CHANGE TO PREVENT IT, AND THE MEASUREMENT KILLED THE PREMISE: the first record in a real delegate transcript is a USER entry carrying the brief, not a tool call, so the file exists on disk before the delegate can invoke anything and the path check answers correctly from its very first call. My repair was an OR of the two signals, which is worse than useless -- with the id present it is unconditionally true, so it reinstates exactly the ROOT-policed-as-delegate bug the override had just fixed. Reverted before commit. THE LESSON IS THE ONE I HAD SPENT THE DAY RECORDING AND STILL BROKE: I read the code, saw a Test-Path returning false on a missing file, and INFERRED a hazard; one look at the first line of a real transcript erased the premise. Reading a failure path tells you what the code does WHEN that state occurs and says nothing about whether that state ever occurs. AND NOTE THE ASYMMETRY THAT MADE IT TEMPTING: the inferred risk was severe -- a delegate writing canonical source -- and severity is exactly what makes an unmeasured premise feel like prudence. The commit said unclassifiable stays ROOT so this can only correct a false positive; that sentence is true in the stop path and is the hazard itself in the write path. THE RULE: before reusing an identity predicate, ask which verdict is the PERMISSIVE one at the new call site, and require the fallback to land on the RESTRICTIVE side. THE COMPOSITION, not the predicate, was the error: an OVERRIDE lets the weaker answer erase the stronger one, while an OR keeps a delegate a delegate when EITHER signal says so, and still frees a ROOT that neither signal accuses. AND THE COMMIT MESSAGE NAMED ITS OWN GAP -- freeing ROOT must not free a real delegate, it said, which is the half a hurried fix drops. THE SAME DISEASE IN THE WRITE GUARDS, located 2026-09-07 and NOT fixed: identity is decided by the mere PRESENCE of a field. Four sites -- wkharness-guards.ps1 at 213, 277 and 584, and wkharness-guards-write.ps1 at 165 -- all read ($script:isSubagent) -or ($j -and $j.agent_id), so ANY value in that field makes the caller a subagent, and each carries a comment asserting ROOT has no agent_id. That assertion is the whole defence and nothing enforces it. It is the twin of the stop-side defect fixed this same day, where a substring in the first user turn was promoted to an identity: both took a WEAK SIGNAL for a NAME, and both wrote a comment describing a protection the code did not have. THE FIX SHAPE IS ALREADY IN THIS REPO -- decide from the transcript PATH SEGMENT, which is structural and cannot be produced by typing. VERIFY IN BOTH DIRECTIONS OR NOT AT ALL: a ROOT session editing CLAUDE.md must be ALLOWED, and a real subagent editing it must STILL be REFUSED; the second case is the one that matters and the one a hurried fix drops. A TRANSCRIPT WITNESS MUST DISTINGUISH AN EXECUTED COMMAND FROM A QUOTED ONE, and the two gates in this repo need OPPOSITE halves of that rule -- get the direction from what the detector is trying to prove. PROVEN ON A LIVE TRANSCRIPT 2026-09-07, and the number is the argument: a session that ran the like command ZERO times scored SEVEN payments when the witness regex was run against its own chatlog. The first id was that-skill, a documentation PLACEHOLDER rather than a real skill; two others were proto-to-live-wiring and agent-brief-standard-template, which are the very ids THE STOP FRAME PRINTS EVERY TURN. So the gate is dissolved by its own harness output -- the frame advertises the skills, the witness reads the advertisement as a receipt, and the debt clears while nobody does anything. A GUARD MUST NOT BE SATISFIABLE BY TEXT THE HARNESS ITSELF EMITS, and the cheapest test for it is to run the witness against a transcript where the act never happened and require ZERO. MEASURED 2026-09-07 on the forced-like witness, found by a real session round after three synthetic fixtures missed it: Get-WkLikedFromChatlog counted a PAYMENT whose first match was not a tool call at all but a line of briefing PROSE, placeholder brackets still in it, so a delegate arrived with its debt already cleared before doing anything. That makes the gate FORGEABLE BY MENTION -- writing the command in a brief, a skill step, a source comment or a chat line clears it -- and forgeable is worse than unwired, because an unwired gate merely fails to fire while a forgeable one fires and is dismissed for free. Its fix is the MIRROR of the rule below: scan ONLY the real tool_use command fields and EXCLUDE text blocks, because it is trying to prove an ACT occurred. TEXT-BLOCK-ONLY SCANNING: every detector in this hook must scan ONLY type-text content blocks extracted via a dedicated regex, never raw tool_use command args or the full joined transcript -- otherwise the hook misreads its OWN commands as if the model itself made the forbidden statement. A FIXTURE THAT CONSULTS LIVE REPOSITORY STATE IS NOT A FIXTURE: its verdict moves when the repo moves, so an ALLOW case fails for a reason having nothing to do with what it tests, and the tally stops being a signal anyone reads. ALWAYS TAKE THE BEFORE BASELINE by checking the file out at the previous commit and re-running, because a previously-red suite and a suite you just broke look identical from one run. The PENALTY half is worse in the other direction: it counts every top-level .tmp proto whose name matches nothing committed, WITHOUT LOOKING AT WHO WROTE IT, so months of predecessor and peer residue are charged to whoever stops next -- measured the same hour at 105 proto-shaped files in a .tmp holding 1438. THE RULE: a counter's LABEL is a claim about what it measures, and it must be read against the code before any session is judged by it or edits a letter to agree with it. FIXED THE SAME DAY, and the fix is one idea worth copying to any repo with a session-scoped metric: BOTH HALVES WERE COUNTING OTHER SESSIONS. GRANTED used the last HANDOFF.md commit as its boundary, and since a session does not commit the letter until its final minute that boundary is DAYS old, so every commit by every other session in between scored as this session's grant. PENALTY counted .tmp protos with no regard for when they appeared, charging months of predecessor and peer residue to whoever stopped next. ONE CURE FOR BOTH: use the TRANSCRIPT FILE'S CREATION TIME as the session clock -- it is the only clock that survives a compaction -- then take git log --since that moment, and count a proto only if its own creation time is newer.
